audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart said 'Skill' for Levels 1 through 6 while the content layer said 'Viktor' for the same rows — the page renders two different answers to who wins each early stage.
audit.why: 45.46% win rate over 1465 games, packet levelChart reads Viktor for rows 0-4, and the content layer already agrees. Viktor's Hextech Ray (525 line, 12/11/10/9/8s) and Gravity Field (800 range, 17/16/15/14/13s) out-range and out-zone pre-Nashor's Azir.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side moved to Viktor with ratings and whys rewritten to match; rows 5 (Azir) and 6 (Skill) already agreed across layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referenced 'Hex Core upgrades' and 'Chaos Storm'; Riot's current text is Hex Fragments (Glorious Evolution) and Arcane Storm.
audit.why: enemyKit passive text: 'Viktor gains Hex Fragments... With every 100 Hex Fragments he obtains, Viktor permanently augments an active ability.' R is named Arcane Storm.
audit.corrected: Renamed throughout; Azir's own spikes (Nashor's Tooth first item, level 6 Emperor's Divide, Rabadon's) left intact and now keyed to Viktor's 120/100/80s R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Enemy E was called 'Death Ray' in four places — the real name is Hextech Ray. The Siphon Power auto-reset tell was never mentioned. Azir's E (Shifting Sands) is a dash Gravity Field's stun punishes, and Arcane Storm is a channel-adjacent zone that Emperor's Divide can separate from your team; none of that reached the page.
audit.why: enemyKit Q flags carry autoReset ('auto-attack reset — burst timing tell') and shield; W carries hardCC + zone; E is a 525-range line, projectile flagged. ownerKit E is dash+shield on 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s; R is terrain on 120/105/90s. missingInteractions flags the Siphon Power auto-reset wind-up as the real cue.
audit.corrected: Hextech Ray used everywhere; cooldowns 17s (W), 12s (E), 22s (Azir E) stated where they make advice concrete; Emperor's Divide framed as separating Arcane Storm's zone from your team.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and named no real number.
audit.why: It is the field that exists to hold cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Gravity Field 17s, Hextech Ray 12s and Azir E 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED). dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d also described something other than their titles.
audit.why: Titles promise a specific action; the bodies explained a different one.
audit.corrected: All four bodies rewritten to match their own titles, grounded in Viktor's ranges and Azir's mana/cooldown costs.

edits.before: W a soldier behind the wave and farm THROUGH it — your auto range is the soldier's range. Don't poke yet; sand costs mana.
edits.after: Viktor's 600-range Siphon Power out-trades your level-1 sand. W behind the wave, farm through the soldier, and spend no mana on poke.

edits.before: Two soldiers up means a real trade: W-Q the drag-through and step back. The poke is free only when his engage is down.
edits.after: Two soldiers let you drag a Q through him, but Gravity Field at 17s still owns the space — trade only right after he spends it.

edits.before: E completes the safety net — you now have the shield-dash out. Greedier soldier placements are allowed, not encouraged.
edits.after: E gives you the shield-dash out, yet Hextech Ray on 10s keeps chipping you from 525 range — farm, do not contest the push.

edits.before: Nashor's components arrive and the soldier DPS starts to sting. Drag Qs through Viktor on every last-hit he takes.
edits.after: Hex Fragments land before your Nashor's does — drag Qs through his last-hit steps but concede the wave and plates.

edits.before: Emperor's Divide online — the dive insurance and the insec flip. With R up you win every 2v2 your jungler joins.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is your dive insurance, but Arcane Storm on 120s zones harder in a 2v2 — fight only with your jungler.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Viktor drops Gravity Field on your feet, stuns you inside it, then finishes with Hextech Ray while your E is down.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. It governs your forward steps. - E Shifting Sands spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Gravity Field is 17s at rank 1: leave the zone as it lands, then step up while it is down. - Hextech Ray is 12s — poke after he spends it. - E Shifting Sands spent on poke is a 22-second death you scheduled. - Hold R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Place the soldier past him, Q it back through his body as he steps to last-hit, auto once through the sand — he eats it or drops the minion.

edits.before: W behind the wave, Q-drag the soldier through Viktor on his last-hit, auto once through the soldier, step back — two-second trades he cannot answer without overextending.
edits.after: Hextech Ray is a 525-range line and Siphon Power reaches 600; your soldier auto reaches past both. Stand behind the sand and never walk up to add your own auto.

edits.before: Viktor whiffs Gravity Field and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Q costs 110 mana at rank 5 — dry mana means no soldiers and no poke.

edits.before: That is Viktor’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Each W is 40 mana on 1.5s; whiffed sand leaves you with nothing to E to.

edits.before: Standing at max soldier range admiring your poke with E on cooldown — that is the engage window every Viktor player is waiting for.
edits.after: Your only exit is E on a 22-second cooldown at rank 1, and Gravity Field stuns anyone who lingers — shoving past river blind is a free setup.

edits.before: Ahead, siege: crash waves with soldier autos, take every plate, and rotate to river with R held — your wall converts even fights into massacres.
edits.after: Ahead, siege: crash with soldier autos, take plates while his 17-second Gravity Field is down, and rotate with R held to wall him off his own storm.

edits.before: Carry through siege control — soldiers take plates, R denies engages, and your DPS curve outlasts every assassin spike in the lobby.
edits.after: Carry through siege — soldiers take plates, and Emperor's Divide walls his team off from Arcane Storm's zone while soldier DPS outlasts it.

edits.after: Play patient and farm safely rather than contesting Hextech Ray poke pre-6

edits.after: Zone you with Gravity Field (W) then poke freely with Hextech Ray (E) to control the wave

edits.before: Viktor's Death Ray (E) and Gravity Field (W) zone control shut down your soldier positioning early, and he clears waves faster than you can contest, letting him push and set up Hex Core upgrades unchallenged.
edits.after: Viktor's Hextech Ray (E) and Gravity Field (W) zone control shut down your soldier positioning early, and he clears waves faster than you can contest, letting him push and bank Hex Fragments unchallenged.

edits.before: Chaos Storm (R) is a devastating teamfight/skirmish tool with huge zone denial, but this is also where Azir starts closing the damage gap thanks to soldier count and R utility, making the lane closer than before.
edits.after: Arcane Storm (R) is a devastating teamfight/skirmish tool with huge zone denial on 120s, but this is where Azir starts closing the gap thanks to soldier count and Emperor's Divide, making the lane closer than before.

edits.before: Late game is genuinely close — Viktor's Chaos Storm zones fights hard but Azir's soldier walls and ultimate provide comparable area control, so this becomes a coinflip decided by positioning and item timing rather than a clean favor either way.
edits.after: Late game is genuinely close — Viktor's Arcane Storm zones fights hard but Azir's soldier walls and Emperor's Divide provide comparable area control, so this becomes a coinflip decided by positioning and item timing rather than a clean favor either way.

edits.before: Level 6 brings Chaos Storm online for him, which is still a strong zone-control ultimate, but this is also the point where your own kit starts to close the gap — soldier count and your ultimate give you comparable area denial for the first time. It's no longer a lost lane, just an even fight where positioning and cooldown tracking matter more than raw stats.
edits.after: Level 6 brings Arcane Storm online for him on a 120-second cooldown, but this is where your own kit starts to close the gap — soldier count and Emperor's Divide give you comparable area denial for the first time. It's no longer a lost lane, just an even fight where positioning and tracking that 120s matter more than raw stats.

edits.before: By full items this becomes a genuine skill matchup — Viktor's Chaos Storm and your soldier walls both zone space effectively, and neither side has a clean statistical edge. Focus on baiting his E poke, tracking his ultimate cooldown, and using your own R to contest zone control in skirmishes and fights.
edits.after: By full items this becomes a genuine skill matchup — Viktor's Arcane Storm and your soldier walls both zone space, and neither side has a clean statistical edge. Bait Hextech Ray out on its 8-second cooldown, track his 80-second ultimate, and use Emperor's Divide to cut his team off from the storm.

edits.before: Viktor simply outclasses you in the early lane — Gravity Field denies your soldier zone control, Death Ray out-ranges your poke, and his wave clear from Hex Core upgrades lets him push you under tower repeatedly. Play passively, prioritize CS over trades, and look to your jungler for help since standing and trading is a losing proposition until your kit catches up.
edits.after: Viktor outclasses you in the early lane — Gravity Field denies your soldier zone control, Hextech Ray out-ranges your poke on a 12-second cooldown at rank 1, and his wave clear pushes you under tower repeatedly. Farm at soldier range, poke only on his last-hit steps, and call your jungler once his 17-second W is spent — trading straight up loses until Nashor's Tooth.
